sourcePolicy: Official ISM monthly reports are authoritative; aggregate diffusion data and selected public respondent comments only. No confidential/raw survey submissions are claimed or used.

releaseStatus.note: August Manufacturing remains the latest official manufacturing report. At this run, August Services has not yet been published; July remains authoritative for Services and no August value is inferred.

industries.interpretation: Breadth remains strong, but demand momentum cooled versus July.

commodities.note: Short-supply list is retained only where explicitly identifiable in the official August ISM publication/review; no private submissions are inferred.

themes: Computer/electronics respondents described an unusually severe supply-chain environment driven by AI infrastructure demand plus war/trade uncertainty.
Machinery comments flagged rapidly rising energy, steel and labor costs while photonics, high-speed connectors, semiconductors and government-related demand remained strong.
Chemical-product comments highlighted tariff and Hormuz-linked inflation risk to customer spending power.
Multiple public comments tied AI-related consumption to component/material scarcity rather than broad finished-goods weakness.

manufacturing.powerStackInterpretation: Still constructive for physical Power Stack demand, but more stagflationary than July: production remains very strong and customer inventories are still too low, while New Orders, Employment and Backlog cooled. Prices stayed at 71.1 and Supplier Deliveries slowed further. The clearest beneficiaries remain real bottlenecks with booked orders and pricing power: grid/electrical equipment, semiconductors/memory, wire/cable, copper-linked supply and industrial automation. The new risk is that high input prices and slower orders expose speculative or unfunded capacity plans.

services.powerStackInterpretation: July Services still shows strong activity/orders but contracting employment and high prices. August Services is due later Sep 3; no value is inferred before the official release.

combinedRead: August Manufacturing remains expansionary but slowed at the margin while inflation/supply-chain pressure stayed intense. The Sep 3 macro cross-check adds weak ADP hiring and extreme refined-product prices, strengthening the quality split: prefer funded, backlog-rich physical infrastructure and scarce components; raise the hurdle for long-duration projects and financed discretionary demand.
